title: Mathematics for Elementary Teaching, II
description: Completes the explanation of elementary school mathematics by discussing geometry and algebra. Discusses the pedagogy with the California mathematics framework, the NCTM standards, and "replacement units".
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 100A.

title: Classical Number Systems
description: A development of classical number systems starting with natural numbers and progressing through the integral, rational, real and complex number systems. Includes an introduction to number theory, mathematical induction, the fundamental theorem of arithmetic and the Euclidean algorithm. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prerequisites_raw: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Mathematical Systems
description: The theory of operations within rings and fields. Polynomials, the fundamental theorem of algebra and other factorization theorems. Analyzing linear, polynomial, rational and exponential functions. Solving algebraic equations and inequalities. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prerequisites_raw: Math 101A with a minimum grade of C.

title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prerequisites_raw: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
prerequisites_raw: Math 102A with a minimum grade of C.

title: Introduction to Group Theory
description: Permutation groups, cyclic groups, theory of finite groups, group homomorphisms and isomorphisms, and Abelian groups. Applications to number theory and geometry.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

title: Introduction Into Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical methods for the solution of nonlinear equations (Newton method), for integration (quadrature formulas and composite integration), and for the initial value problem for ordinary differential equations (Euler and Kutta methods).
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 4B or 4BI, 6A, and 6B; and, Math 8 or PSTAT 8, and Math 117 and, Computer Science 5AA-ZZ or 10 or 8 or 16 or Engineering 3, each with a grade of C or above.

title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical methods for the solution of systems of linear equations (direct and iteractive methods), and the finite difference methods for boundary value problems for (ordinary and partial) differential equations.
prerequisites_raw: Math 104A with a minimum grade of C.

title: Advanced Topics in Numerical Analysis
description: Topics in approximation theory; numerical methods for finding eigenvalues of a matrix; and advanced topics in numerical methods for ordinary and partial differential equations.
prerequisites_raw: Math 104B with a minimum grade of C.

title: Linear Algebra
description: Abstract vector spaces and subspaces. Span and linear independence. Basis and dimension. Linear maps. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
prerequisites_raw: Math 4A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.

title: Linear Algebra
description: Diagonalization, inner product spaces, projections, least-squares approximations, invariant factors and elementary divisors, canonical forms, topics from advanced matrix theory, applied linear algebra, and group representation theory.
prerequisites_raw: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.

title: Matrix Analysis
description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and similarity; Unitary equivalence and normal matrices; QR factorization; Least squares; Singular Value decomposition; Moore-Penrose generalized inverse; Hermitian and symmetric matrices; Variational characterization of eigenvalues; Positive definite matrices; Nonnegative matrices; Perron-Frobenius Theorem.
prerequisites_raw: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C

title: Abstract Algebra
description: An introduction to group theory, focusing on finite groups. Basic algebraic concepts including homomorphisms, normal subgroups, quotients, direct products and group actions. Classification of finitely generated Abelian groups. Other topics such as semidirect products and Sylow theorems as time permits.
prerequisites_raw: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.

title: Abstract Algebra
description: Ring theory, ideals, factorization. Examples include number rings and polynomial rings. Module theory if time permits.
prerequisites_raw: Math 111A with a minimum grade of C.

title: Abstract Algebra
description: Fields, field extensions, Galois theory.
prerequisites_raw: Math 111B with a minimum grade of C.

title: Non-euclidean Geometry
description: An introduction to hyperbolic geometry with some discussion of other non-euclidean systems.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

title: Computational Tools for Numerical Analysis
description: Introduction to programming with specific examples in scientific computing. The algorithms used will be analyzed in detail in Math 104A-B-C. The emphasis will be the translation of numerical algorithms into actual working code.
prerequisites_raw: Math 6B, Math 8, and Math 108A or Math 117 each with a letter grade of "C" or higher.

title: Introduction to Number Theory
description: Number-theoretic functions, divisibility, congruences, primitive roots and indices, quadratic residues and the quadratic reciprocity law.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

title: Introduction to Number Theory
description: Selected topics at the discretion of the instructor. Possibilities include (but are not limited to) Diophantine equations, the distribution of primes, number-theoretic methods in cryptography, quadratic forms, continued fractions, algebraic number theory, and partitions.
prerequisites_raw: Math 115A with a minimum grade of C.

title: Topics in Number Theory
description: Selected topics in number theory at the direction of the instructor.
prerequisites_raw: Math 115B with a minimum grade of C or consent of instructor.

title: Combinatorial Analysis
description: Elementary counting principles, binomial coefficients, generating functions, recurrence relations, the principle of inclusion and exclusion, distributions and partitions, systems of distinct representatives, applications to computation.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

title: Methods of Analysis
description: Introduction to methods of proof in analysis. topics include limits, sequences and series, continuity, compactness, as well as other topics. This course is intended to follow Mathematics 8 and to introduce students to the level of sophistication of upper-division mathematics.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 8 or PSTAT 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

title: Real Analysis
description: Axioms of the real numbers, topology of metric spaces, numerical sequences, infinite series.
prerequisites_raw: Math 4B, 6A, 108A and 117, each with a minimum grade of C.

title: Real Analysis
description: Real functions: continuity, differentiability, Riemann integrals, power and trigonometric series.
prerequisites_raw: Math 108B and 118A, each with a minimum grade of C.

title: Real Analysis
description: Multivariable calculus and a selection of other topics including differential forms or Lebesgue integral.
prerequisites_raw: Math 118B with a minimum grade of C.

title: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Existence, uniqueness, and stability; the geometry of phase space; linear systems and hyperbolicity; maps and diffeomorphisms.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 4B or 4BI and 6A with a minimum grade of C; and Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.

title: Chaotic Dynamics and Bifurcation Theory
description: Hyperbolic structure and chaos; center manifolds; bifurcation theory; and the Feigenbaum and Ruelle-Takens cascades to strange attractors.
prerequisites_raw: Mathematics 6B and Math 119A, each with a minimum grade of C
